pages.text:
“Analysis of Urine Dilutions on the Growth of
Swiss Chard in 50/50 Earth-Lunar Simulant”
The MAJOR MOONERS
8th Grade Participants
Grace Lutheran School
Pocatello, Idaho
December 2024
BACKGROUND/REASONING: Why did you choose your experiment category (Moon simulant) and your particular
independent and dependent variables?
Two years ago our school celebrated the launch of Artemis I and was excited to follow the journey back
to our moon. We chose the lunar simulant because we are following the Artemis mission and excited to
contribute in whatever way possible. We considered what it would take to grow food for astronauts in space
and didn’t want to add to the payload, so we researched low-cost, sustainable and renewable gardening
methods. Using urine as a fertilizer would allow the astronauts to recycle their waste and conserve precious
cargo room. Therefore, we agreed to use urine dilutions as the independent variables in our experiment.
Urine as a fertilizer has been utilized for many years worldwide. Rather than flushing urine away, it
could be used to supply precious minerals and nutrients to plants like nitrogen, phosphorus,
potassium, magnesium, calcium, and sulfur. According to the Rich Earth Institute, one gallon of urine contains
0.05 pounds of nitrogen, 0.008 pounds of phosphorus, and 0.017 pounds of potassium.
In another study
reported by Peter Morgan, urine was applied to several crops including spinach and other nitrogen loving
plants and plant growth was up to seven times improved. They used a 1:3 urine dilution and applied it more
frequently than our plans could accommodate.
We were also wary about using too much urine as that could
cause nutrient burn and harm the plants.
The dependent variables were chosen based on the idea that the following plant growth parameters,
plant height, leaf and stem length, number and color of leaves and overall plant mass, would show
improvement with the addition of urine because of its high nitrogen and mineral value. Nikhil Kishor et al.
reported diluted urine at 30% improved plant leaf growth and amount of chlorophyll, which we understood to be
leaf growth. Looking at photographs in other studies like Peter Morgan’s, we noticed that the increase in plant
mass was visually evident.
Initially, we were interested in studying spinach because it has been used in a variety of space
gardening experiments because of its reliability and nutritional value. We then discovered Swiss Chard as an
alternative because it had a very similar germination rate but was not day-length responsive, meaning it would
not bolt if subject to changing environmental conditions like light and temperature. Swiss Chard is hearty, easy
to grow, and offers more vitamin C, choline and B5 than spinach. Finally, it offers the astronauts a variety!
VARIABLES:
INDEPENDENT VARIABLE(s): The independent variables are the additions of urine as a fertilizer due
to its high nitrogen content. The following dilutions of urine with distilled water will be applied to the
seedlings twice during the growing period: Distilled water (control), Undiluted urine, 1:1, 1:4 and 1:8.
DEPENDENT VARIABLE(s): The dependent variable is the observed growth of the Swiss Chard
seeds. This will be measured as the height of the plant (cm), length of longest leaves (cm), length of
stem (cm), number and color of leaves, final plant mass and overall health.

CONTROLS/CONSTANTS:
* soil mixture (50/50 lunar regolith simulant & Miracle Grow Garden Soil: Vegetable & Herbs)
* 300 grams of soil mixture per pot
* filtered water from fountain (all pots received the same amount of water)
* two seeds per pot planted at a depth of 1/2 inch
* same light, temperature and humidity exposure
* Swiss Chard Ruby Red (Beta vulgaris subsp. vulgaris) from Organo Republic www.organorepublic.com
HYPOTHESIS:
We think that by adding diluted urine as a source of nitrogen will enhance the growth of swiss chard because
swiss chard is a nitrogen-needy plant. Urine is an excellent fertilizer when used correctly. According to the Rich
Earth Institute, no standard urine:water dilution exists but a range of 1:3 to 1:5 is the most common. Therefore, we
hypothesized that the 1:4 dilution will work best without the fear of overfertilizing the plants.
EXPERIMENTAL RATIONAL: What is the overall value your experiment brings to the scientific community?
By experimenting with alternative fertilizers, lunar soils, and various vegetable species, we aim to
provide the scientific community with innovative options for establishing living colonies on the moon. A 50/50
mix of lunar simulant and Earth soil can minimally support plant growth. However, when supplemented with a
1:1 urine-to-water additive, the plants exhibited robust growth. Even weaker dilutions demonstrated enhanced
growth compared to no fertilizer at all.
Urine is an economical and accessible fertilizer that should not be overlooked. The students involved in
this study dedicated their time and effort in the hope that their findings will contribute to future experiments and
support advancements in space exploration and sustainable farming.

PROCEDURES: Describe the grow setup, schedule and method your team used to test the hypothesis and record data.
SET UP
●
Put on our masks and gloves and
prep a draft free area to mix soils.
●
Using a digital scale, measure and
thoroughly mix 1500 grams each of
lunar regolith and Miracle Grow soil
creating 3000 grams of soil mixture.
●
Measure 300 grams of soil per pot
and label each pair of pots as follows:
control, 1:1 urine, 1:4 urine, 1:8 urine,
pure urine.
●
Plant 2 SWISS CHARD seeds 1/2
inch into each pot using a marked
glass rod.
●
Water each pot with 20 ml of water.
Spray each surface 10 times.
●
Put pots inside the classroom
greenhouse. Monitor each pot for
signs of germination and moisture
levels.
MAINTENANCE/
WEEKLY PROTOCOL
●
Water plants Mon-Wed-Fri using
graduated cylinders and filtered water
from the hall fountain. Amount will
change as needed with all pots
receiving the same amount each time.
Average increase was about 10 ml
per week.
●
Record the following when watering:
volume of water in mL, temperature
degrees F using digital thermometer,
% humidity using the digital thermometer, pH using the probe, germination and interesting observations.
●
Record the following data on Wednesdays into data chart: plant height (cm), stem height (cm), longest
leaf length (cm), # of leaves, leaf color, and overall health.
●
Clean up area.
FINAL DATA GATHERING
●
Each plant was trimmed at the very base and the mass was measured immediately in gram to lessen the
effects of water loss. Our balance only measured the whole number. Averages were calculated.
EXPERIMENT
●
Obtain 100 ml clean, sterile urine sample (from a drug/medicine free adult) for use that day. Freeze the
rest for the second application.
●
The amendments were created using the following ratios:
Pure Urine (U1-2)
1:8 (U3-4)
1:4 (U5-6)
1:1 (U7-8)
Control (CA, CB)
—-
40 ml distilled water
20 ml distilled water
15 ml distilled water
20 ml distilled water
20 ml urine
5 ml urine
5 ml urine
15 ml urine
—
●
Use a plastic pipette to apply 20 ml of the amendment, 1 inch deep into the soil so that the urine does not
evaporate and/or smell.
●
Repeat one week after initial application using thawed urine sample. Our application weeks were 5 & 6 as
we wanted to fertilize once they were well established.
DATA COLLECTION: List and organize your results.

ANALYSIS: Summarize and draw meaning from your findings and results.
The pure urine and 1:1 dilution showed the
tallest plant growth. The plant without any urine
was the shortest. Even though the plants were
equidistant from the light source, this value
wasn’t as important to us because leaf growth
would offer more nutritional value to astronauts.
We were pleased to see that the control (no
urine) had the lowest average of leaves per plant
and the 1:1 urine dilution had the most.
Interestingly enough the 1:4 dilution (our
hypothesis) had the same as no urine at all and
the other dilutions ranked at varying degrees.
This confused us- and more research would
need to be done to explain this data set.
Interestingly, the plant without any fertilizer
showed the longest stem growth. This took the
students by surprise! They came to understand
the descriptive term “legginess” as a plant is
striving to reach the light source. The controls
were exposed to the exact amount of light as the
others, so it was probably due to nutrient
deficiency. All dilutions of urine had nearly the
same effect on stem length.

Interestingly enough the 1:4 dilution (our hypothesis) had the same as no urine at all and the other dilutions ranked at varying degrees. This confused us- and more research would need to be done to explain this data set.

Interestingly, the plant without any fertilizer showed the longest stem growth. This took the students by surprise! They came to understand the descriptive term “legginess” as a plant is striving to reach the light source. The controls were exposed to the exact amount of light as the others, so it was probably due to nutrient deficiency. All dilutions of urine had nearly the same effect on stem length.

We were excited to see that the average longest
leaf length belonged to the plants with the 1:4
urine dilution, but shared that place with the 1:1
dilution as well.
The plant with straight urine showed second to
smallest average leaf length. This we
understood as too much nitrogen that can
interfere with photosynthetic activity.
The final average plant masses showed that the
1:1 dilution produced more plant mass than any
other dilution. We were happy to see that the
1:4 dilution was next, and it was no surprise to
see the plant with no urine have the lowest
mass.
CONCLUSIONS: Reflect on the season- what did you learn? What’s the coolest thing you discovered?
Our data did not support our hypothesis, as the 1:4 urine-to-distilled-water ratio did not have the most
significant positive effect on the growth of Swiss chard plants. Instead, the 1:1 urine dilution yielded the best
results, producing the highest wet mass, the longest leaves, and the greatest number of leaves.
The students gained valuable insights through this experiment. Many found it fascinating to learn how
urine can benefit plant growth, even though using it was initially considered “awkward” for middle school
students. One student was particularly impressed by the ability of a simple 50/50 mix of lunar simulant and
Earth soil to support plant growth, especially after researching the challenging properties of lunar regolith, such
as its pH and soil structure.
During the growing phase, students observed how plants respond to environmental factors like light
and temperature. For example, the control plants, which lacked any fertilizer, became “leggier,” indicating they
were stretching their stems to move their leaves closer to the light source and improve photosynthetic activity.
FUTURE CONSIDERATIONS: What changes or improvements would you consider if you repeated the experiment?
Since this was the first time conducting an experiment requiring precise measurements over a long
period, we honored everyone’s request to collect plant measurements. To reduce human error and
inconsistencies, we would plan to assign specific persons to handle measurements. We also propose to
fertilize the Swiss Chard plants weekly using pooled human urine samples. In this experiment, we only had one
sample which allowed us to fertilize twice. Acquiring different samples would accurately reflect the situation
astronauts would face. With the understanding that a 1:1 urine-to-water dilution produced the best results for
Swiss chard, we are interested in testing its effectiveness on varying lunar simulant-to-Earth soil ratios. For fun,
the students want to test the 1:1 dilution on 100% lunar simulant.
tables: We were excited to see that the average longest leaf length belonged to the plants with the 1:4 urine dilution, but shared that place with the 1:1 dilution as well. The plant with straight urine showed second to smallest average leaf length. This we understood as too much nitrogen that can interfere with photosynthetic activity.

The final average plant masses showed that the 1:1 dilution produced more plant mass than any other dilution. We were happy to see that the 1:4 dilution was next, and it was no surprise to see the plant with no urine have the lowest mass.

pages.text:
Most students were intrigued by the fact that Swiss Chard is a ‘cold hearty’ plant and wondered what
would happen if we changed the temperatures while using a 1:1 urine:water dilution. Our experimental setting
was on the warm side with temperatures between 69 and 73 degrees F. It was discussed that a lunar capsule
would have stable temperatures between 65 and 70 degrees F and the chard might fare better.
The discussion extended beyond growing crops inside a lunar module to the possibility of cultivating
crops directly on the moon’s surface in a gardening ‘pod.’ They learned that the day/night cycle on the moon
would be about two weeks and proposed another experiment simulating the moon’s light/day cycle.They also
considered how to accommodate the great temperature changes a lunar environment would entail..
